set.st: Harris Schultz, aged 62 (an earlier OCR read "12") lived alone in Springbrook [Spencer Brook] township near Cambridge and was found dead in September 1914. He was afraid to keep his money in banks, and it was supposed that several thousand dollars were buried somewhere near his home. His only known relative was a sister in Minneapolis, and a search was to be made. "Springbrook" in the Cambridge wire story is a garble of Spencer Brook Twp beside Cambridge (Kanabec Co has no such township); no follow-up found through 1917. Pin is on his 25 acres in sec 6 from the 1914 atlas farm directory, not the spot itself. An earlier LiDAR check (USGS 1 m, 2022) found a cellar-sized pit, about 21 x 14 m and 0.9 m deep, at 45.50732,-93.44124 near the old township pin; the 1914 atlas shows other owners there, so it is probably not his. Records check: Princeton Union, Sept. 24, 1914: Harris Schultz was found dead in his home 'at the old Emerson farm in Spencer Brook', where he lived alone; neighbors noticed his stock neglected. An Emerson name on a Spencer Brook Twp. plat or patent would place the farm.
set.t: 1914 Webb atlas farm directory: 25 ac in sec 6 Spencer Brook Twp; the Rum River crosses the S part of the section, so the land is probably an unlabelled river piece. Check the 1938-40 aerial for a house site there, and later papers for whether the money was found. Permission: private land.
set.pl: 1914 atlas farm directory: 25 ac in sec 6 Spencer Brook Twp, by the Rum River.
pinev: Section-part level: the 1914 Webb Isanti atlas farm directory lists him with 25 ac in sec 6 T35N R25W; the Rum River crosses the S part of sec 6, so the pin is there (about 600 m). Neither the old township pin nor the LiDAR pit has his parcel in the 1914 atlas.
